accepted.name: events_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  event_date,
  event_timestamp,
  event_name,
  event_previous_timestamp,
  event_value_in_usd,
  event_bundle_sequence_id,
  user_id,
  user_pseudo_id,
  user_first_touch_timestamp,
  device.category AS device_category,
  device.mobile_brand_name AS device_mobile_brand_name,
  device.mobile_model_name AS device_mobile_model_name,
  device.operating_system AS device_operating_system,
  device.time_zone_offset_seconds AS device_time_zone_offset_seconds,
  geo.country AS geo_country,
  geo.region AS geo_region,
  geo.city AS geo_city,
  app_info.id AS app_id,
  app_info.version AS app_version,
  traffic_source.source AS traffic_source_source,
  traffic_source.medium AS traffic_source_medium,
  platform,
  ecommerce.transaction_id AS ecommerce_transaction_id,
  ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd AS ecommerce_purchase_revenue_in_usd,
  ecommerce.purchase_revenue AS ecommerce_purchase_revenue,
  ecommerce.total_item_quantity AS ecommerce_total_item_quantity,
  ecommerce.unique_items AS ecommerce_unique_items,
  event_params,
  user_properties,
  items
FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`
grain: one row per event row in a shard (event_date + event_timestamp + event_bundle_sequence_id + user_pseudo_id)

semantic_filters._TABLE_SUFFIX: use BETWEEN or IN to restrict date range in outer query

accepted.description: Normalized, event-level projection that preserves primary identifiers and commonly-used descriptive and measure columns. Use this as the canonical starting relation for downstream joins, aggregations, ranking and reshaping. Includes table suffix so callers can restrict date ranges with _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN ... | Use for: Basic event counts and funnels; Daily revenue / purchase metrics; Filtering events by device/geo/traffic_source/platform; Prepping for UNNEST of items or event_params

accepted.name: events_params_kv
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  event_date,
  event_timestamp,
  event_bundle_sequence_id,
  user_pseudo_id,
  event_name,
  param.key AS param_key,
  COALESCE(param.value.string_value, CAST(param.value.int_value AS STRING), CAST(param.value.double_value AS STRING), CAST(param.value.float_value AS STRING)) AS param_value_string,
  param.value.int_value AS param_value_int,
  param.value.float_value AS param_value_float
FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`,
UNNEST(event_params) AS param
grain: one row per event_param (event * param key)

semantic_filters._TABLE_SUFFIX: use BETWEEN or IN to restrict date range in outer query

accepted.description: Unnested event parameters as one row per event_param key/value. Use to filter or aggregate by event param keys, or to pivot param values back into event-level with conditional aggregates. Preserves event identifiers to join back to events. | Use for: Filter events by specific event_param key/value; Pivot event_params into event-level columns; Count occurrences of param values over time

accepted.name: daily_event_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  event_date,
  event_name,
  COUNT(1) AS events_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_pseudo_id) AS unique_users,
  SUM(event_value_in_usd) AS sum_event_value_in_usd,
  SUM(ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd) AS sum_ecommerce_purchase_revenue_in_usd,
  SUM(ecommerce.total_item_quantity) AS sum_ecommerce_total_item_quantity
FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`
GROUP BY _TABLE_SUFFIX, event_date, event_name

semantic_filters._TABLE_SUFFIX: use BETWEEN or IN to restrict date range in outer query

accepted.description: Daily aggregated counts and basic revenue sums by event_date and event_name. Useful for time series of event volumes and revenues. Aggregates at the shard/event_date grain; callers should restrict _TABLE_SUFFIX to control the date window. | Use for: Daily event volume and revenue trends; Comparing event types by day; Feeding dashboards with daily aggregates

accepted.name: user_last_event_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  event_date,
  user_pseudo_id,
  event_timestamp,
  event_bundle_sequence_id,
  event_name,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_pseudo_id ORDER BY event_timestamp DESC, event_bundle_sequence_id DESC) AS rn,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_pseudo_id ORDER BY event_timestamp DESC) AS rnk
FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`
grain: one row per event with rank columns per user_pseudo_id

semantic_filters._TABLE_SUFFIX: use BETWEEN or IN to restrict date range in outer query

accepted.description: Per-user ranking of events by event_timestamp within the scanned shards. Exposes row_number and rank so callers can filter down to most recent or N-most-recent events per user. Preserve table_suffix to allow date windowing. | Use for: Find most recent event(s) per user; Sessionization start/end heuristics; Select top-N recent events per user

accepted.name: user_cumulative_revenue
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  event_date,
  user_pseudo_id,
  event_timestamp,
  COALESCE(ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd, 0) AS purchase_revenue_in_usd,
  SUM(COALESCE(ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY user_pseudo_id ORDER BY event_timestamp ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_revenue_in_usd
FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`
grain: one row per event with cumulative running total per user_pseudo_id ordered by event_timestamp

semantic_filters._TABLE_SUFFIX: use BETWEEN or IN to restrict date range in outer query

accepted.description: Per-user running total of ecommerce purchase revenue (USD) ordered by event_timestamp. Useful to compute lifetime-to-date revenue per user across scanned shards. Keep table_suffix filter externally to bound the time range. | Use for: Compute LTV over a window; Detect when user crosses revenue thresholds; Plot cumulative revenue per user or cohort

accepted.name: top_items_by_revenue_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  table_suffix,
  event_date,
  item_id,
  item_name,
  SUM(COALESCE(item_revenue_in_usd, item_revenue, 0)) AS total_item_revenue,
  SUM(COALESCE(item_quantity, 0)) AS total_item_quantity,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY table_suffix, event_date ORDER BY SUM(COALESCE(item_revenue_in_usd, item_revenue, 0)) DESC) AS item_revenue_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
    event_date,
    items.item_id AS item_id,
    items.item_name AS item_name,
    items.item_revenue_in_usd AS item_revenue_in_usd,
    items.item_revenue AS item_revenue,
    items.quantity AS item_quantity
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`,
  UNNEST(items) AS items
)
GROUP BY table_suffix, event_date, item_id, item_name

semantic_filters._TABLE_SUFFIX: use BETWEEN or IN to restrict date range in outer query

accepted.description: Item-level revenue ranking per day: aggregates item revenue by table_suffix and event_date then computes rank ordered by revenue descending. Exposes item_revenue_rank so callers can filter to top-K per day. | Use for: Top-N items by revenue per day; Daily item performance reports; Feeding top-items to dashboards (filter WHERE item_revenue_rank <= K)

accepted.name: user_event_sequences
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  base._TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  base.event_date AS event_date,
  base.user_pseudo_id AS user_pseudo_id,
  base.event_timestamp AS event_timestamp,
  base.event_name AS event_name,
  next_event.event_timestamp AS next_event_timestamp,
  next_event.event_name AS next_event_name,
  SAFE_CAST(next_event.event_timestamp - base.event_timestamp AS INT64) AS seconds_to_next_event
FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*` AS base
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*` AS next_event
  ON base.user_pseudo_id = next_event.user_pseudo_id
  AND next_event.event_timestamp > base.event_timestamp
grain: one row per base event (may multiply if multiple later events exist); intended for nearest-neighbor when combined with WHERE to pick smallest positive gap

semantic_filters._TABLE_SUFFIX: use BETWEEN or IN to restrict date range in outer query

accepted.description: Self-join style relation to pair each event with the next event for the same user ordered by timestamp. Produces one row per preceding event with next-event attributes (lead) to support simple journey and transition analyses. Use table_suffix filter externally to bound the time window. | Use for: Event-to-event transition times; Simple next-event funnels; User journey step counting (when combined with windowing or grouping to choose nearest next)
